# Sacramento Kings 2026-27 NBA Season Preview - Avoid Relegation

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-07-31, 44:22. https://youtu.be/oEywzBZfAvY

## Summary

Josh Lloyd and James Ham preview the 2026-27 Sacramento Kings. They describe a team in the middle of a teardown and rebuild, built around number 7 pick Darius Acuff Jr. Ham calls Domantas Sabonis the best player and Zach LaVine the second best. Both hope the offense runs through Sabonis again, and they expect LaVine to look better without Westbrook, Schroder and DeRozan taking the ball. Keegan Murray's shooting and offensive role are the big question marks. Malik Monk is the backup point guard, but the backcourt plays no defense. Doug Christie is under the most pressure, and both hosts predict about 26 wins while the team tries to avoid the bottom-three relegation zone.

## Rules and methods

- [5:19](https://youtu.be/oEywzBZfAvY?t=319) Don't judge rookies on Summer League. They play next to other fringe players, and opposing defenses go all out to disrupt them.
  > "when at Summer League, it it's not a good representation of who you're going to be on the court"
- [14:17](https://youtu.be/oEywzBZfAvY?t=857) A player's numbers depend on who is around him. Taking away ball-dominant teammates can raise a player's usage and production.
  > "it's going to make him just look better by having the different players around him who make more sense"
- [13:32](https://youtu.be/oEywzBZfAvY?t=812) Under the new lottery relegation zone, being one of the three worst teams is a penalty, so bottom teams have a reason to try to win games.
  > "the relegation zone in this year's uh you know, NBA draft lottery where you don't want to be one of the three worst teams"
- [40:57](https://youtu.be/oEywzBZfAvY?t=2457) When one team in a weak group loses a key player to injury, it can lose several wins. Other bad teams can then pick up those extra wins.
  > "an injury that occurs will just it set one team down five, six, seven wins"
- [34:33](https://youtu.be/oEywzBZfAvY?t=2073) A coach fighting for his job may lean on veterans to win games instead of developing young players.
  > "does he really rely on these four veterans in the starting lineup and just kind of push the other guys to the side"
